question: Our coated ECM scaffold suppressed myofibroblast conversion in one run and promoted it in the repeat. Which explanation should we test first, before the coating formulation is frozen?
goal: Pick the single next cell-level experiment that would actually resolve the contradiction, given that the two runs differ in more than the coating.

context.cell_type_in_question: adult human dermal fibroblast, abdominal skin, donor 2, passage 6
context.cell_type_in_repeat_run: neonatal human dermal fibroblast, foreskin, donor 5, passage 3
context.system: 2D on scaffold, single cell type, no in vivo arm

constraints: single cell type only, for cost and time
one further experiment before the formulation is frozen
no new donor can be sourced in time

evidence.statement: alpha-SMA positive fraction was lower on the coated scaffold than on uncoated at day 14
evidence.measurement_context: immunofluorescence, n=3, coated and uncoated in the same plate, adult abdominal donor 2 at passage 6, scaffold lot A, operator 1, not blinded

evidence.statement: In the repeat run the coated scaffold showed a higher alpha-SMA positive fraction than uncoated at day 14
evidence.measurement_context: immunofluorescence, n=3, neonatal foreskin donor 5 at passage 3, scaffold lot B, operator 2, not blinded

evidence.statement: The coated scaffold measured about 11 kPa and the uncoated about 26 kPa
evidence.measurement_context: nanoindentation, n=5 positions, hydrated, scaffold lot A only; lot B was never measured

evidence.statement: The coating suppresses myofibroblast conversion by lowering the stiffness the cells experience
assumptions: lot B has the same coated-versus-uncoated stiffness difference as lot A
nanoindentation stiffness is what the cell senses on this surface

evidence.statement: Growth factor released from an ECM scaffold as it degrades is a common alternative driver of myofibroblast conversion, independent of stiffness
assumptions: nothing in this session has measured release from either lot
